tools.name: search_addresses
tools.description: Use when you have a UK postcode and need the exact property (broadband availability differs per property). Ask for the postcode and house number or name in ONE question up front. If the user's message already identifies the property (e.g. '1 Fyfields, SS13 1HJ'), match it against the returned list y

tools.name: find_broadband_deals
tools.description: Use when the user wants broadband deals, offers or packages available where they live. If the user has not picked an address yet, call search_addresses first and offer the list; fall back to postcode-only search when they decline or no addresses are found (the precision field says which you got). tools.name: check_if_overpaying
tools.description: Use when the user asks whether their CURRENT broadband bill or plan, or a RENEWAL or retention offer their provider quoted, is expensive, competitive or worth switching from. Compares what they pay against comparable deals actually available at their address and returns a computed verdict with true

tools.name: get_deal_details
tools.description: Use when the user asks for more detail about ONE specific deal already returned by another tool: setup costs, price-rise terms, what happens after the intro period and availability at their address. Pass the deal_id from the earlier result, plus the user's postcode, uprn and address_label when known

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "standard" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_addresses, find_broadband_deals · Public sink: find_broadband_deals.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_addresses, find_broadband_deals · Public sink: find_broadband_deals

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
